nodes.name: ZIF-L Crystallization
nodes.procedure: A piece of CC with a size of 30mm×40mm×0.36mm was firstly washed with acetone ultrasonically to remove the oily pollutant. Then the CC was immersed into a mixed acid solution containing concentrated nitric acid (HNO3, 10 mL) and concentrated sulfuric acid (H2SO4, 30 mL) for 24 h. The as-obtained CC was washed with deionized water and ethanol several times to ensure the surface of the CC was well cleaned before used. After that, the CC substrate supported by stent was immersed in distilled water (H2O, 50 mL) with 2-methylimidazole (1.313 g, 16 mmol) and Co(NO3)2·6H2O (0.583 g, 2 mmol) for 2 h at room temperature (25°C) to obtain ZIF-L on CC (named as CC@ZIF-L). Furthermore, the as-obtained CC@ZIF-L sample with a light purple color was washed with H2O for several times until the water turned colorless before further used and further dried in an oven at 60°C for 24 h.
nodes.source_text: 5.1 Synthesis of CC@ZIF-L ... immersed in distilled water (H2O, 50 mL) with 2-methylimidazole (1.313 g, 16 mmol) and Co(NO3)2·6H2O (0.583 g, 2 mmol) for 2 h at room temperature (25°C)

nodes.name: Ion-exchange Etching
nodes.procedure: Firstly, Ni(NO3)2·6H2O (0.29 g, 1 mmol) was dissolved in anhydrous ethanol (C2H6O, 50 mL). Next, a piece of CC@ZIF-L was immersed into the as-prepared Ni-solution stationarily for 60 min at room temperature. Finally, the as-obtained CC@CoNiLDH sample with light green color was washed with ethanol for several times and finally dried at 60°C in vacuum for 24 h.
nodes.source_text: 5.2 Synthesis of CC@CoNi-LDH ... Ni(NO3)2·6H2O (0.29 g, 1 mmol) was dissolved in anhydrous ethanol ... immersed into the as-prepared Ni-solution stationarily for 60 min at room temperature

nodes.name: Urea-assisted Pyrolysis
nodes.procedure: The as-obtained CC@CoNi-LDH and urea powder (0.5 g) were placed at the center and the upstream side positions of a tube furnace, respectively. Next, the samples were pyrolyzed under Ar atmosphere first at 160°C for 2 h, and then to 600°C for 2 h with a ramping rate of 5°C·min⁻¹. After pyrolysis, the black sample (named as CC@CoNi-NC) can be obtained.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM reveals CC@CoNi-LDH with rough surface and hollow interior after ion-exchange etching; CC@CoNi-NC inherits hollow structure with CoNi NPs on surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figs. 2(a1), 2(a2), 2(b1), and 2(b2), the transformation from CC@ZIF-L with smooth surface to CoNi-LDH with rough surface can be clearly observed... The hollow interior of the CC@CoNi-LDH arrays can be clearly observed in the SEM images of the milled sample.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms hollow structure of CC@CoNi-LDH by dark edge shell/bright core contrast; CC@CoNi-NC shows CoNi NPs in carbon matrix and nanotubes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: which can also be confirmed by the contrast between the dark edge shell and the bright core in the TEM images (Figs. 2(a3) and 2(b4)).

nodes.characterization_summary: CC@CoNi-LDH: 0.24 nm (012) plane; CC@CoNi-NC: 0.34 nm graphitic carbon (002), 0.206 nm CoNi alloy (111).
nodes.evidence_snippet: HRTEM images of CC@CoNi-NC clearly show two different interplanar spacings of 0.34 nm for the outer carbon layers and 0.206 nm for the inner CoNi nanoparticle, which can be assigned to the (002) lattice plane of graphitic carbon and the (111) lattice plane of CoNi alloy, respectively (Fig. 2(c4)).

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM and EDS reveal homogeneous distributions of Co, Ni, and O in CC@CoNi-LDH; rich distributions of Co, Ni, C, N in CC@CoNi-NC hollow shell with CoNi NPs on nanotubes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-angle annular dark-field scanning TEM (HAADF-STEM) and the corresponding energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) elemental distribution images reveal the homogenous distributions of Co, Ni, and O in CoNi-LDH (Figs. 2(b6) and 2(b7)).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping confirms elemental distributions in CC@CoNi-LDH and CC@CoNi-NC; line scanning shows CoNi alloying in nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HAADF-STEM and the corresponding EDS mapping images of CC@CoNi-NC further reveal the rich distributions of Co, Ni, C, and N in its hollow shell, while some CoNi NPs are also decorated on the end side of nanotubes (Figs. 2(c5) and 2(c6)).

nodes.characterization_summary: CC@CoNi-LDH: (003) at 11.21° (PDF 33-0429); CC@CoNi-NC: CoNi alloy (111) at 44.2°, (200) at 51.6°.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the XRD pattern of CC@CoNi-LDH displays a new diffraction peak at 11.21°, which can be indexed to the (003) crystal planes of CoNi-LDH (PDF No. 33-0429)... the resultant CC@CoNi-NC shows two peaks at 44.2° and 51.6° located between those of Co and Ni.

nodes.characterization_summary: CC@CoNi-LDH: 467 cm⁻¹ (Ni-OH/Co-OH), 534 cm⁻¹ (Ni-O/Co-O); CC@CoNi-NC: D-band 1335 cm⁻¹, G-band 1590 cm⁻¹, I_D/I_G ≈ 0.96.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the Raman spectrum of CC@CoNi-LDH also exhibits two new obvious characteristic peaks at 467 and 534 cm⁻¹... the Raman spectroscopy can well prove the formation of crystalline carbon in CC@CoNi-NC with two distinguishable peaks at approximately 1335 and 1590 cm⁻¹... I_D/I_G ratio of CC@CoNi-NC is measured to be ∼0.96.

In high-resolution Co 2p XPS spectra, several Co species including Co-N (797.9 and 782.1 eV), Co-O (796.5 and 780.7 eV), and Co-Co (794.0 and 778.9 eV)... Similarly, in the high-resolution Ni 2p XPS spectrum of CC@CoNi-NC, two new types of Ni states assigned to Ni-N (872.4 and 855.8 eV) and Ni-Ni (870.9 and 853.7 eV).

nodes.characterization_summary: CC@CoNi-LDH: reversible Ni²⁺/Ni³⁺ redox at 1.18 V_RHE; C_dl = 198.3 mF·cm⁻², ECSA = 0.50 m² for CC@CoNi-NC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: a reversible redox curve (Ni²⁺/Ni³⁺) can be observed in a typical cyclic voltammetry (CV) scanning of CC@CoNi-LDH... CC@CoNi-NC still exhibits the highest ECSA of 0.50 m² with the C_dl of 198.3 mF·cm⁻².

nodes.characterization_summary: CC@CoNi-NC: R_ct = 1.1 Ω (smallest charge transfer resistance).
nodes.evidence_snippet: the Nyquist plots obtained from electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) tests... confirm the fastest electrode/electrolyte interfacial electronic transfer kinetics of CC@CoNi-NC with the smallest charge transfer resistance (R_ct) of 1.1 Ω.
